record.context_brief: Typical contingent zero-forcing size in power-grid-like graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with structural properties characteristic of power grids, and let k≥0. A set Z⊂V is an (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set if it remains zero-forcing after deletion of any set of at most k edges. Determine the typical size of a minimum (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set, expressed in terms of the numbers of vertices and edges, for graphs with power-grid-like structure.

evidence.quote: Definition 7.3 ((n − k)-contingent Zero Forcing). Given a graph G = (V, E), a set Z ⊆ V is a (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set if for every set of edges E0 of size at most k, Z is a zero-forcing set for G0 = (V, E − E0).

Open Problem 7.3. What is the typical size, in terms of the number of vertices and edges, of the minimal (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing sets in graphs exhibiting structural properties characteristic of power grids?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph on n = |V| vertices. The standard zero-forcing process on G with initial set Z ⊆ V proceeds as follows: each vertex of Z is colored blue, all others white; repeatedly, if a blue vertex v has exactly one white neighbor u, then u is colored blue (the "color-change rule"). The set Z is a zero-forcing set if iterating this rule eventually colors every vertex of V blue.

For an integer k ≥ 0, call Z ⊆ V an (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set of G if, for every subset E₀ ⊆ E with |E₀| ≤ k, the set Z is a zero-forcing set of the edge-deleted graph G − E₀ = (V, E ∖ E₀). Let Z_{n−k}(G) denote the minimum cardinality of an (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set of G.

Consider random or deterministic families of graphs that model the structural properties characteristic of electrical power-grid networks (e.g., sparse graphs with heavy-tailed or bounded degree distributions, planar or near-planar embeddings, and small treewidth typical of transmission networks). Determine the typical (asymptotic) value of Z_{n−k}(G) for such graphs as a function of the number of vertices n and the number of edges m = |E| (and of k).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a 2023 survey on applied combinatorics. Web searches return general material on N−k contingency analysis in power systems but no results that determine, asymptotically or otherwise, the typical minimum size of (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing sets in power-grid-like graphs. No published resolution was found.
